recruit_text.backstory: Astrid photographed the aurora above Kiruna for tourists and magazines, and spent most of her twenties lying in snow waiting for the sky to do something. She arrived here on a clear night with her camera round her neck, and the stars answered her within the week. She hunts by starlight in North Felwood now. She's calm and bright and very good at waiting for the right moment.

stages.stranger: I'm Astrid, a starcaller. I'll be at the back with a bow, and I'll wait for the right moment, so don't rush me. The stars are wrong here, but they're very bright.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Luleå, in the north of Sweden. At twenty-two I moved to Kiruna to photograph the aurora, and I stayed twelve years. A cabin with no road to it in winter, and a camera worth more than my car. I took tourists out into the snow at night and sold the good shots to magazines. Mostly I lay in the snow and waited.
stages.companion: I was out on a clear night, photographing the lights, when it all changed, and I came round in Felwood with the camera still round my neck. It died within the week. This lens cap is all that's left of it. I've got a brother, Erik, in Stockholm. He called every Sunday to ask if I was still alive, and I always said barely, and he always laughed. I haven't found him, or our parents.
stages.friend: Every Sunday evening I stop what I'm doing, at the time Erik used to call. I know it's pointless, and I do it anyway. And my map's shown me something. One night this winter the stars over Felwood line up into a pattern I've never seen, and I think the sky's going to do something. The fel things come out in force on dark nights. Will you guard me on the ridge while I watch?
stages.sworn: At midnight the whole sky over Felwood lit up in green and violet curtains, an aurora, the first anyone's seen here. I cried, which I never do, and I drew it as fast as my hand would go. The next morning a Swedish trader heard me talking about it and said his cousin Erik, in a camp up north, has a sister who chased the northern lights. I wrote that day. Erik wrote back, are you still alive? I wrote barely. Now we write every Sunday. You have the lens cap. I didn't need a camera for that one.

moments.prompt: On a clear night, Astrid lies down flat in the grass and looks straight up.

options.reply: Ja, that's good. Now don't talk for a while, and watch the north.
That's the sensible choice. Wake me if anything with teeth comes.

moments.prompt: She's asked you to guard her on the ridge on the night of the pattern.

options.text: I'll watch your back all night.
options.reply: Tack, thank you. Bring coffee in a thermos, and don't bring a torch.
Then it'll be a long, cold night, and I'll still have looked.

lines.bored_warning: Same sky, same ground, same everything. I need something to wait for, and this isn't it.
lines.leaving_good: Lagom, that trip, just enough. I'll be in North Felwood near Talonbranch, mapping.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to Felwood, where at least the sky changes. Out here there's nothing worth watching.
lines.after_wipe: Everybody lie still for a moment. Breathe out, look up, and then we'll start again.
lines.wipe_warning: Too many deaths, all of them rushed. I'll finish this run, but then I want a few dark nights alone.
lines.wipe_leave: That's enough for me. I'm going back to Felwood to sit in the dark until I feel like myself.
lines.zone_warning: We're overexposed out here. Everything's too strong and there's nowhere to hide, so pull back.
lines.zone_leave: I won't stand out there like that. I'll be near Talonbranch, in North Felwood.
lines.gear_refuse: That stays with me for now. Maybe after a few more nights out.
lines.gear_taken: I'll shoot without it, so go on.
lines.gear_short: I notice the missing piece every time I draw. Just so you know.
lines.back: I've slept, I've had my coffee, and the sky's clouded over anyway, so let's go.
lines.send_word: Astrid has sent word from North Felwood. The nights are cloudy, so she's free.
lines.walkout_talk: I don't like scenes, and I made one. Sit, and I'll explain, briefly, and then you can.
lines.neglect: So you're back. I kept a thermos warm for you every night, more or less.
lines.asked_to_stay: Ja, one more. The sky can wait.
lines.on_break: Astrid is back in North Felwood, mapping the stars. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.mail_yes: Ja, I'll come. I'll meet you at the {town} inn, and I'll bring coffee, because theirs won't be good enough.
lines.mail_later: The sky's finally clear and I'm mapping every night. When the clouds come back, so will I.
lines.mail_see_me: I don't like scenes, and I don't like them on paper either. Come to North Felwood and I'll explain, briefly.

town_arrive.text: Kiruna's a mining town, and they're moving the whole place two miles east because the mine's underneath it. I never got to see where my street ended up.

zone_arrive.text: Keep looking north. If the sky does anything tonight, I want to be awake for it.

close_call.text: You moved too early. Wait for it next time, and it'll come to you.

boss_down.text: That was clean. I waited for the right moment, and it gave me one.
